# `m.stocks.daily_open_close`

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

The open, close, and pre- and after-market prices of US stocks on one day.

```python
m.stocks.daily_open_close(symbols, date, *, adjusted=True)
```

[All datasets](README.md)

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Verbs | `fetch()`, `poll()` |
| Served by | REST |
| `poll()` | holds exactly the latest cycle's rows, keyed by `Symbol` (`dm.PollMode.REPLACE`) |

## Plan access

Which of Massive's plans include this dataset, how recent its data is on each, and how far back its history goes, as Massive's pages state them.

| Plan | Daily Ticker Summary (OHLC) (REST) |
| --- | --- |
| Stocks Basic | End-of-day, 2 years |
| Stocks Starter | 15-minute delayed, 5 years |
| Stocks Developer | 15-minute delayed, 10 years |
| Stocks Advanced | Real-time, All history |
| Stocks Business | Real-time, All history |

## Columns

| Column | Deephaven type | Description | Supplied by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Symbol` | String | The instrument, in the library's canonical symbol form. From REST `symbol`: "The exchange symbol that this item is traded under." | REST |
| `Date` | String | The day the summary covers, as ISO yyyy-MM-dd text: a New York calendar day. From REST `from`: "The requested date." | REST |
| `TimestampStart` | Instant | The start of the day the summary covers, as an Instant: 00:00 New York time of `Date`. | REST |
| `TimestampEnd` | Instant | The exclusive end of the day the summary covers, as an Instant: 00:00 New York time of the next day. | REST |
| `RawSymbol` | String | The symbol exactly as Massive sent it, on a row whose spelling the library cannot read as the dataset's class (its `Symbol` is then null); null on every other row. Present unless the session's `unreadable_symbols` is `dm.OnError.RAISE`, which fails on such a row instead. | REST |
| `Open` | double | The open price for the symbol in the given time period. Split-adjusted when the query's adjusted is True, the default, served only by REST: a price from before a split is restated in the split's terms (divided by its ratio), so it is not the price that traded. With adjusted=False, from the flat files, and on the WebSocket it is as traded. One history() never mixes the two, and Massive never adjusts for cash dividends. | REST |
| `High` | double | The highest price for the symbol in the given time period. Split-adjusted when the query's adjusted is True, the default, served only by REST: a price from before a split is restated in the split's terms (divided by its ratio), so it is not the price that traded. With adjusted=False, from the flat files, and on the WebSocket it is as traded. One history() never mixes the two, and Massive never adjusts for cash dividends. | REST |
| `Low` | double | The lowest price for the symbol in the given time period. Split-adjusted when the query's adjusted is True, the default, served only by REST: a price from before a split is restated in the split's terms (divided by its ratio), so it is not the price that traded. With adjusted=False, from the flat files, and on the WebSocket it is as traded. One history() never mixes the two, and Massive never adjusts for cash dividends. | REST |
| `Close` | double | The close price for the symbol in the given time period. Split-adjusted when the query's adjusted is True, the default, served only by REST: a price from before a split is restated in the split's terms (divided by its ratio), so it is not the price that traded. With adjusted=False, from the flat files, and on the WebSocket it is as traded. One history() never mixes the two, and Massive never adjusts for cash dividends. | REST |
| `Volume` | double | The trading volume of the symbol in the given time period. Split-adjusted like the prices when the query's adjusted is True, the default, served only by REST: a volume from before a split is restated in the split's terms (multiplied by its ratio). With adjusted=False, from the flat files, and on the WebSocket it is as traded. | REST |
| `AfterHours` | double | The close price of the ticker symbol in after hours trading. Split-adjusted when the query's adjusted is True, the default, served only by REST: a price from before a split is restated in the split's terms (divided by its ratio), so it is not the price that traded. With adjusted=False, from the flat files, and on the WebSocket it is as traded. One history() never mixes the two, and Massive never adjusts for cash dividends. | REST |
| `Otc` | boolean | Whether or not this aggregate is for an OTC ticker. This field will be left off if false. | REST |
| `PreMarket` | double | The open price of the ticker symbol in pre-market trading. Split-adjusted when the query's adjusted is True, the default, served only by REST: a price from before a split is restated in the split's terms (divided by its ratio), so it is not the price that traded. With adjusted=False, from the flat files, and on the WebSocket it is as traded. One history() never mixes the two, and Massive never adjusts for cash dividends. | REST |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, as an Instant: the local clock when the REST page, flat-file block, or WebSocket frame that carried it arrived, the same for every row of one. It is not monotonic and is not Massive's own receive time; on history() rows it is the download time, and in a poll() table the latest poll's. | REST |

`RawSymbol` holds Massive's spelling of a symbol the library cannot read; that row's `Symbol` is null, and `RawSymbol` is null on every other row. A session with `unreadable_symbols=dm.OnError.RAISE` (in code or in the settings file, as `unreadable_symbols: raise`) fails on such a row instead and has no `RawSymbol`; the table shows the default session.
